data.title: Bulk Transfer to Personal Cloud Storage Unrestricted
data.summary:
Large volumes of corporate data were uploaded to consumer cloud storage accounts from
managed devices. The destinations are widely used legitimate services, and no control
distinguished corporate from personal accounts.
data.description:
Consumer storage is the most convenient exfiltration route available, because the traffic
is to a reputable provider over a normal protocol and is indistinguishable in transit from
sanctioned use of the same service.

The common control failure is blocking by domain. The corporate tenant and a personal
account of the same provider usually share hostnames, so a block removes a business
capability without removing the exfiltration route, and is quickly reversed. Tenant
restriction headers — which allow the organisation's tenant while refusing others — are
the control that actually distinguishes them, and they are frequently not deployed.

This route is also the one most often used by departing employees, so the control has
value well beyond the red team scenario that exposed it.
data.recommendation:
* Enforce tenant restrictions at the proxy for major cloud providers, allowing the
  corporate tenant and refusing personal accounts of the same service.
* Alert on upload volume to cloud storage per user, which catches providers not covered by
  tenant restriction.
* Review which storage services have a business justification and refuse the remainder by
  default rather than by exception.
data.short_recommendation: Enforce tenant restrictions rather than blocking cloud storage by domain.
